cells: Advise government on telecom policies and licensing.

blocks.content: The recommendations of TRAI are advisory in nature and not binding on the Central Government.

rows: Disputes between licensor, licensees, and consumers

items: TRAI's recommendations regarding the need and timing for introduction of new service providers are advisory and non-binding.
TDSAT was set up in 2000 to adjudicate disputes between a licensor and a licensee, between two or more service providers, and between a service provider and a group of consumers.
Members of TRAI hold office for a term of 3 years or until they attain the age of 65 years, whichever is earlier.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: TRAI was established as a statutory body under the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997.
The 2000 Amendment separated adjudicatory functions from TRAI and established the Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT).
TRAI regulates telecommunication services, including fixation and revision of tariffs for telecom services.
The authority consists of a Chairperson and not more than two full-time members and two part-time members.
